notes: Coverage refers to reported hulls: inclusive for calibrated belts, outward-rounded (one grid node beyond the accepted nodes, within Θ) for the exact core FC and WALDO belts; raw disconnected-set diagnostics are separate.
Exact core FC and WALDO coverage checks use a mu scan of step 0.001, on and between the construction nodes; on_node_minimum_coverage is the coverage-grid minimum.
Finite calibration/nuisance grids and Monte Carlo checks do not establish continuous-domain coverage.
Core central and upper-limit procedures assume known b; selecting one after seeing data can break coverage.
Flat equal-tail credible intervals have zero endpoint coverage in the enumerated core check, up to the reported count-tail error.
Naive Wald is a deliberately failing small-count baseline; its coverage-check failure is expected.
fc_core uses FC's non-increasing-in-b correction for every count (auxiliary b grid 0..25, step 0.01), as in the published FC tables.
Core WALDO uses a local exact posterior; full WALDO provenance is recorded separately.
Default calibration checks b in [0.5,10] and eps in eps0*exp([-2,-1,0,1,2]*sigma_eps); this bounded coverage box does not truncate the unbounded reality prior.
The eps0-only calibration ablation ignores an efficiency nuisance; its independent box coverage failures are retained.
Calibration quantile error is separate from the reported coverage toy error.
Most points of the main and efficiency check grids are calibration nodes (calibration_node_overlap); random_box_check tests random points off the nodes.
Reported minima are minima of many noisy estimates and are biased low; reestimated_minima gives fresh-toy estimates at the lowest points.
The pass rule certifies coverage of about 0.885 or more at the checked points; pass_rule_characteristic gives its exact operating characteristic.
The gzip artifact preserves the complete version-1 payload, including per-point arrays.
interval_summary reports reality-prior averages; maximum rates report grid extrema.
Disconnected rates use initial full-case toys where recorded; null means not recorded.
Bounds summarize the checked domain; exact grid nodes and reruns are in the details.
